name: Static soliton of five dimensional gravity
description: A neutral static vacuum family with a radially varying fifth dimension.
convention: We take $x^0=ct$ for components and keep $c$ explicit in the line element. The fifth direction is spacelike, and the exponents obey $a^2+ab+b^2=1$.
history: The circumference of a compact fifth dimension varies with distance from a static spherical source. Its local size acts as a scalar field in four dimensions, coupled to the curvature of spacetime [kramer1971projective]. The five dimensional geometry satisfies the vacuum Einstein equations, and its diagonal form carries zero electric and magnetic charge [lake2006static]. The circle approaches a constant circumference at spatial infinity [lake2006static].¶Dietrich Kramer constructed the static spherical family in 1971 while studying projective field theory [kramer1971projective]. He related its scalar field equations to those of a massless scalar through a conformal rescaling and wrote the spherical solution explicitly. Alan Chodos and Steven Detweiler obtained the broader family of solutions with spherical symmetry and a translation symmetry along the fifth dimension in 1982 [chodos1982]. Their time independent solutions allow electric and scalar charge in addition to mass [overduin1997].¶David J. Gross and Malcolm J. Perry wrote the neutral family in isotropic coordinates in 1983 [grossperry1983, lake2006static]. Aharon Davidson and David A. Owen studied the changing size of its compact fifth dimension in 1985 [davidsonowen1985]. The family has a length scale and one independent dimensionless parameter [lake2006static]. For a radial coordinate $r$ and a positive length $r_s$, write $f=1-r_s/r$; the time and circle coefficients are $g_{tt}=-f^a$ and $g_{yy}=f^b$, with $a^2+ab+b^2=1$ [overduin1997].¶Two points on this ellipse have a regular inner boundary [lake2006static]. At $a=1$, $b=0$, the fifth dimension has constant size and the geometry is Schwarzschild's black string. Its horizon extends along the fifth dimension. At $a=0$, $b=1$, time separates from the Euclidean Schwarzschild geometry, and the circle closes smoothly at $r=r_s$ when the coordinate $y$ has period $4\pi r_s$. The latter solution has constant $g_{tt}=-1$, so a particle released from rest remains at rest.¶At the other points, curvature diverges at the inner endpoint, and radial light rays expose the singularity to the exterior [lake2006static]. Kayll Lake classified these geometries in 2006 using coordinates adapted to their two orthogonal Killing vectors. The area of the symmetry spheres may shrink to zero or pass through a minimum before growing without bound toward the singularity. Reduction along the fifth dimension and a conformal rescaling yield the spherical geometry of a massless scalar field, whose exponent $\gamma=a+b/2$ obeys $\gamma^2=1-3b^2/4$ [kramer1971projective].

coordinates.name: Spherical
coordinates.convention: We use $(t,r,\theta,\phi,y)$, with $t$ a time, $r$ and $y$ lengths, and $\theta$ and $\phi$ angles.

parameters.description: Dimensionless circle exponent on the same ellipse.

coordinates.convention: We use $(t,h,\theta,\phi,y)$, with $t$ a time, $y$ a length, and $h$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ dimensionless.

related.text: At $a=1$, $b=0$, the circle has constant size and the solution is the uniform Schwarzschild black string [lake2006static].
Reduction along $y$ and a conformal rescaling produce the massless scalar geometry with exponent $\gamma=a+b/2$, for $0<\gamma<1$ [kramer1971projective].
The norm of the fifth translation acts as a scalar field in four dimensions, and the mixed metric components supply the gauge potential [overduin1997].
Gross and Perry studied the neutral scalar family and magnetic monopoles in five dimensional vacuum gravity [grossperry1983, lake2006static].
